title: gop evidence graph (gop.graph/v2)
description: graph.json written by gop collect. The Go source of truth is internal/graph/types.go. Unknown fields and attribute keys are allowed so additive changes stay within v2; consumers must ignore what they do not know.

audit_retention_days.description: Audit log retention (days) the audit facts were read under. When set, audit edges older than half of it are stale by default.

org_collected_at.description: Optional. When each org's facts were last read, keyed by org login (RFC 3339). A merge of a re-collection of some orgs into an older graph keeps the older time for the other orgs.

Evidence.description: How a fact was observed. inferred means derived from other observed facts by a documented rule (attrs.rule names it); it counts as confirmed. not_visible means unknown, not absent. supplied means read from a file the user supplied (a cloud OIDC trust policy); gop did not observe it live.

Attrs.description: Flat string attributes. Unknown keys are allowed.

attr_evidence.description: Per-attribute evidence where it differs from evidence.

NodeAttrs.description: Node attributes. Known keys are typed below; unknown keys are allowed.

ip_allow_list_entries.description: org: number of active IP allow list entries (org owner only); entry values are never collected.

ip_allow_list_apps.description: org: whether the IP allow list also applies to installed GitHub Apps (org owner only).

ref_protected.description: action_ref on a branch: whether branch protection stops a pusher from changing it alone.

ref_protection.description: Comma list of the branch's rules, e.g. reviews,dismiss_stale,status_checks.

bypass.description: Comma list of principal IDs that can land code on the protected branch, or move the immutable tag, alone; none, or unknown.

ref_kind_source.description: action_ref: api when ref_kind was looked up, name when it is the name heuristic (a fallback).

ref_ambiguous.description: action_ref: the ref name is both a tag and a branch (ref_kind is then branch).

ref_immutable.description: action_ref with ref_kind=tag from the API: whether pushing alone cannot move the tag.

ref_immutable_reason.description: Why ref_immutable is true: an immutable release, or a tag ruleset with update and deletion rules.

token_write.description: workflow: whether its GITHUB_TOKEN has contents: write on its own repo (unknown when the default workflow permissions are not visible).

token_scopes.description: workflow: comma list of the token's other write scopes, e.g. id-token,packages, or write-all. Display only.

risky_triggers.description: workflow: comma list of its triggers that run in the base repo's context on events people without push access can cause (pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, ...).

actions_lock.description: repo: true when gop read a .github/workflows/actions.lock (gh actions-lock); unknown when one is listed but could not be read or parsed. Absent: no lockfile.

actions_access.description: Repo hosting a referenced action: its Actions access setting (who outside the repo may use its actions), public for public repos, or unknown.

source.description: Where the node's facts came from: the API label on an org found outside the enterprise listing; cartography on a cloud_target that a CAN_ASSUME edge from a Cartography export points to.

account.description: cloud_target: AWS account, GCP project or Azure subscription, when the trust file names it.

role.description: cloud_target: role name, GCP service account or Azure identity.

warnings.description: cloud_target: comma list of risk codes from the trust, e.g. no_sub_condition, no_aud_condition, wildcard_owner, unparsed_condition.

poutine_rules.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the poutine rule IDs with a finding in this workflow file (gop enrich --poutine). Cited from poutine, not proved by gop.

poutine_severity.description: workflow: the highest poutine rule level among those findings.

poutine_jobs.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the job ids the poutine findings name.

poutine_file.description: workflow: the poutine report the findings were read from.

agent.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the AI coding agent kinds it runs (claude-code-action, codex-cli, ...), or unknown for a name-only match. See docs/agents-in-ci.md.

agent_source.description: workflow: sorted comma list of how the agents were found: uses (a known action), run (a known CLI in a run: step), image (a known agent platform image as the job container, a service or a docker:// step), setup (the Copilot setup workflow), heuristic (a step holds a model API key and reads the pull request's content), name (only the name looks like an agent); composite, reusable or script when the agent is one level down (in a local composite action, a called reusable workflow, or a repo script a run: step invokes).

agent_confidence.description: workflow: the strongest agent signal. heuristic: a step holds a model API key and reads the pull request's content (its CAN_TRIGGER edges are not_visible). name_only never makes a path agentic.

agent_jobs.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the agent job ids.

agent_gate.description: workflow: the weakest actor check of its agent steps: write_access, listed_users, anyone, none (no check) or unknown (gop does not know the action's check).

agent_exposure.description: workflow: who can start an agent job with the base repo's token and secrets: outsiders (people without push access, on a risky trigger), listed_users, fork_readonly (a fork's pull_request: read-only token, no secrets) or maintainers.

agent_prompt_injection.description: workflow: sorted comma list of attacker-controlled contexts interpolated into the agent steps (with:, env: or run:), and pr_content when an LLM step found by heuristic reads the pull request's files, diff or text.

untrusted_checkout.description: workflow: it checks out the pull request's head under a risky trigger. exec: a later step runs code from that checkout (a CAN_TRIGGER edge with exec=checkout); read_only: gop sees no step that does, so it is untrusted input, not execution.

agent_permissions.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the agent jobs' token write scopes (contents:write, id-token:write, write-all, ...), or default when a job takes the repo default.

agent_secrets.description: workflow: number of secrets the agent jobs reference (GITHUB_TOKEN excluded), integer as string.

agent_runner.description: workflow: the agent jobs' riskiest runner class.

agent_tools.description: workflow: sorted comma list of agent tool and sandbox settings: allowed_tools, or a value that removes the agent's approval or sandbox (dangerously_skip_permissions, bypass_permissions, yolo, full_auto, ...).

agent_ref_kind.description: workflow: the least pinned ref kind of its agent actions.

advisories.description: action_ref: comma list of the OSV advisory IDs (GitHub Actions ecosystem) that affect this ref, e.g. a known compromise. Set only for affected refs.

advisory_severity.description: action_ref with advisories: the highest advisory severity.

advisory_fixed.description: action_ref with advisories: the first fixed version that leaves every listed advisory; absent when one has no fix.

branch_protected.description: repo: whether classic branch protection or an active ruleset applies to the default branch; unknown when the rules could not be read (never read as unprotected).

branch_required_reviews.description: repo: approving reviews the default branch requires (the highest over classic protection and rulesets), or unknown.

branch_code_owner_review.description: repo: a source requires code owner review on the default branch.

branch_dismiss_stale.description: repo: a source dismisses stale approvals on push.

branch_last_push_approval.description: repo: a source requires the last push to be approved by someone else.

branch_status_checks.description: repo: distinct required status checks on the default branch, or unknown.

branch_signed_commits.description: repo: a source requires signed commits.

branch_allow_force_push.description: repo: force pushes to the default branch are allowed (no source blocks them).

branch_push_restricted.description: repo: a source restricts who may push (classic push restrictions or an update rule).

branch_bypass_actors.description: repo: bypass actors over all protecting sources (ruleset bypass actors and classic pull request bypass allowances), or unknown.

branch_admin_bypass.description: repo: repo or org admins get past every protecting source (classic without enforce_admins, rulesets with an admin bypass actor).

branch_app_bypass.description: repo: an app gets past every protecting source.

branch_bypass_apps.description: repo: when branch_app_bypass is true, the GitHub Apps that get past every protecting source, as a sorted comma list of <app id> or <app id>:<slug>; absent when gop could not list them (gop redact replaces each App with app-<hash>).

branch_protection_sources.description: repo: comma list of the protecting sources (classic, ruleset:<id>), or none.

branch_value_sources.description: repo: which source set each effective value, comma list of key=source[+source], e.g. required_reviews=ruleset:7.

codeowners.description: repo: the CODEOWNERS file GitHub uses on the default branch (the first of .github/, root, docs/), none, or unknown.

codeowners_valid.description: repo: false when a CODEOWNERS line has syntax GitHub skips.

codeowners_workflows.description: repo: the CODEOWNERS rule matching .github/workflows/ files names an owner.

secret_scanning.description: repo: secret scanning, from security_and_analysis (shown to repo admins, org owners and security managers).

bot_approves.description: workflow: a job submits an approving pull request review (gh pr review --approve, the reviews API with event APPROVE, an approve action, or an agent allowed to run gh pr review). See docs/agents-in-ci.md.

bot_approve_token.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the approving steps' token sources: app, pat, github_token, unknown.

bot_approve_jobs.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the approving job ids.

bot_approve_starter.description: workflow: the widest population that can make an approving job run.

bot_merges.description: workflow: a job merges a pull request (gh pr merge, the merge API, an automerge action).

bot_merge_token.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the merging steps' token sources: app, pat, github_token, unknown.

bot_merge_jobs.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the merging job ids.

bot_merge_starter.description: workflow: the widest population that can make a merging job run.

bot_merge_gate.description: workflow: the merging job's actor check.

bot_merge_triggers.description: workflow: sorted comma list of the triggers that start a merging job.

review_bypass.description: repo: bot_self_merge when a pull request's author can get it approved and merged by bots with no human review (not_visible when possible only).

review_bypass_reason.description: repo: why the bot merge needs no human review.

review_bypass_approve.description: repo: sorted comma list of the approving workflow files.

bot_merge_source.description: workflow, repo: script:<path> when the merge call is in a repo script a workflow step runs (read from the default branch, never executed); absent when the merge is a workflow step.

bot_approve_source.description: workflow: script:<path> when the approve call is in a repo script a workflow step runs.

bot_merge_stale_approvals.description: workflow, repo: suspected when the merge script seems to count approvals not tied to the head commit (a dismissed review, or a review of an older commit it does not skip). A heuristic, never confirmed: attr evidence not_visible, with a bot_merge_stale_approvals coverage entry.

bot_merge_stale_confidence.description: workflow, repo: the confidence of bot_merge_stale_approvals.

review_bypass_stale_approval.description: repo: suspected when the merge counts older approvals (suspected) and an approving workflow does not re-run on synchronize: the approval may not cover the merged code.

agent_holds_merge_key.description: repo: an AI agent step's env (or with:) holds the same secret the bot merge's token comes from.

agent_merge_key_workflows.description: repo: sorted comma list of the workflow files whose agent step holds the merge key.

bot_merge_apps.description: workflow, repo: sorted comma list of the GitHub Apps the merging steps' App tokens are for: the app id or slug the workflow names literally (an App token step's with:, or an APP_ID beside a private key in the step env), or unknown for an App it does not name (a vars. or secrets. reference); gop redact replaces each App with app-<hash>.

actions_can_approve_prs.description: repo: the "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" setting (can_approve_pull_request_reviews), read only for a repo with a bot approval made with GITHUB_TOKEN; unknown (not_visible, with an actions_can_approve_prs coverage entry) when gop could not read it.

review_bypass_app_match.description: repo, app_bypass only: matched (live) when an App the merge mints for is a bypass actor of the default branch rules; unmatched or unknown (not_visible: the review bypass is possible only) otherwise.

review_bypass_recounts_dismissed.description: repo: suspected when the default branch rules dismiss stale reviews and the merge script counts DISMISSED reviews: the script re-counts approvals GitHub dismissed. A heuristic, never confirmed: attr evidence not_visible.

EdgeAttrs.description: Edge attributes. Known keys are typed below; unknown keys are allowed.

rule.description: Inferred edges: the rule that derived the fact from other observed facts, e.g. default_perm, org_owner.

via.description: CAN_PUSH provenance, e.g. default_perm, org_owner, direct, outside_collaborator, team, ref_bypass, token_write, unknown (not_visible edges to repos gop did not collect). New values may be added within v2.

jobs.description: Comma list of job ids: those a via=token_write CAN_PUSH edge comes from, or those that can mint the token on an EXECUTES_WITH edge to oidc.

environments.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: comma list of the id-token jobs' environment names; *dynamic* for an expression.

job_workflow_ref.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: comma list of called reusable workflows that mint the token, as owner/repo/path@ref.

repository.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: the token's repository claim, owner/repo.

repository_owner.description: EXECUTES_WITH to oidc: the token's repository_owner claim.

ref.description: Branch or tag a via=ref_bypass CAN_PUSH edge applies to.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the workflow or action file the edge was read from.

file_ref.description: Commit or branch the file was read at, when known.

trigger.description: CAN_TRIGGER: the risky trigger the principal can cause, e.g. pull_request_target. CAN_MERGE_VIA_BOT: the trigger that starts the merge.

approve_workflows.description: CAN_MERGE_VIA_BOT: sorted comma list of the approving workflow node IDs; absent when no approval is needed.

merge_workflow.description: CAN_MERGE_VIA_BOT: the merging workflow node ID.

review_bypass_reason.description: CAN_MERGE_VIA_BOT: why the bot merge needs no human review.

exec.description: CAN_TRIGGER: how the workflow runs attacker input: checkout, injection, or agent (an AI coding agent reads attacker text and acts with the job's token, secrets and tools).

author_association.description: CAN_TRIGGER: comma list of the author_association values the job's if: allows on a comment or review trigger. MEMBER narrows who can trigger to the org's members; CONTRIBUTOR includes outside contributors.

actions_lock.description: USES edge from a workflow in a repo with an actions.lock: locked when the lockfile pins it (and every nested ref gop saw), stale when it does not (counts as unpinned).

locked_sha.description: USES edge with actions_lock=locked: the commit the lockfile pins.

lock_entry.description: USES edge with actions_lock=stale: comma list of the lockfile's pin keys (owner/repo@ref) for the same action repo.

lock_missing.description: USES edge with actions_lock=stale: comma list of the nested refs (owner/repo@ref) the lockfile does not pin for this workflow.

lock_advisories.description: USES edge with actions_lock=locked: comma list of the advisory IDs that list locked_sha as affected. Describes the locked commit only; the action node's advisories attrs stay the ref-level match.

lock_advisory_severity.description: USES edge with lock_advisories: the highest severity among them.

lock_advisory_fixed.description: USES edge with lock_advisories: the first fixed version that leaves every one of them; absent when one has no fix.

consumer_org.description: USES edge into an enterprise-hosted action: org of the using workflow or action.

matched_sub.description: CAN_ASSUME: comma list of the trust's sub patterns that matched.

claims.description: CAN_ASSUME: comma list of the claims the trust checks.

pointer.description: CAN_ASSUME: JSON pointer of the trust inside the supplied file.

oidc.description: CAN_ASSUME: the oidc node whose token the trust matches.

reason.description: CAN_ASSUME with evidence not_visible: why gop cannot decide the match.

trust.description: CAN_ASSUME: the trust's own target when it names more than the cloud_target (an Azure federated credential).

source.description: CAN_ASSUME: cartography when the trust came from a Cartography export (gop enrich --cartography); absent for trust files.

observed_use.description: CAN_ASSUME: CloudTrail, through a Cartography export, saw a workflow of this repo assume the role.

times_used.description: CAN_ASSUME with observed_use: number of AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity calls in Cartography's CloudTrail window, integer as string.

last_used.description: CAN_ASSUME with observed_use: time of the last such call, as the export gives it.
